subtitle: How Mysore Turned the Kaveri into a Modern Sea

panels.shot: epic wide of the massive KRS dam with water stretching to the horizon and the silhouettes of Visvesvaraya and Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV in the foreground
panels.action: M. Visvesvaraya stands beside Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV on the crest of the completed KRS dam, both gazing over the vast shimmering reservoir that has swallowed the old valley, with the Mysore countryside and distant hills under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: In Mysore’s age of experiments, M. Visvesvaraya and Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV dared to raise a sea from the Kaveri’s flow — and almost saw their dream washed away before it stood.

i18n.hi: मैसूर के तजुर्बों के दौर में, एम. विश्वेश्वरैया और कृष्णराज वोडेयार चतुर्थ ने कावेरी की धारा से समुंदर उठाने की हिम्मत की — और बनने से पहले ही सपना बह जाता दिखा।

panels.shot: tight two-shot in a dim palace study, lamplight on maps and faces
panels.action: A younger Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV sits at an ornate desk in Mysore Palace, brow furrowed over a large survey map of the Kaveri basin, while M. Visvesvaraya stands beside him, pointing to Kannambadi with a rolled blueprint in hand.

dialogue.text: In 1911, in a quiet palace room far from the roar of the Kaveri, a young Maharaja and his Diwan traced a line on a map that would drown villages and feed cities.

i18n.hi: १९११ में, कावेरी के शोर से दूर, महल के एक सन्नाटे वाले कमरे में, नौजवान महाराजा और उनके दीवान ने नक्शे पर वो लकीर खींची जो गाँव डुबोकर शहरों को खिलाएगी।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Visvesvaraya looking down at the map dotted with canals and a dam-line
panels.action: The map on the table shows the Kaveri winding past Kannambadi, with a bold pencil line across it for the proposed dam and branching canal lines towards Mandya and distant Mysore city; Visvesvaraya’s finger rests firmly on the dam site as the Maharaja watches intently.

dialogue.speaker: M. Visvesvaraya
dialogue.text: Highness, one wall here can turn seasons of flood into years of grain.

i18n.hi: महराज, यहाँ की एक दीवार, बरसों की बाढ़ को अनाज के सालों में बदल सकती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of the Maharaja straightening in his chair, decision in his eyes
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV leans back, palms pressed together in thought, then looks up at Visvesvaraya with a calm yet firm expression as the lamplight catches the edges of scattered engineering drawings.

dialogue.text: Mysore was already called a ‘model state’, its ruler eager for schools, mills, and power. But a dam of this scale risked treasure, reputation, and the wrath of those downstream.

i18n.hi: मैसूर पहले ही ‘आदर्श राज्य’ कहलाता था, शासक स्कूलों, मिलों और बिजली को उतावला। पर इतने बड़े बाँध पर खजाना, इज़्ज़त, और नीचे बहने वालों का ग़ुस्सा दाँव पर था।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Kaveri at Kannambadi, wild and untamed, under monsoon clouds
panels.action: The Kaveri river churns broad and fast at Kannambadi, its muddy surface broken by rocks and swirling eddies, with small village houses and palm trees lining the banks and thunderclouds gathering overhead.

dialogue.text: Down in the valley, the Kaveri had carved her own path for ages, rushing past Kannambadi’s fields, ignoring the earlier dream of Tipu, whose unbuilt dam lived only in memory and a plaque.

i18n.hi: घाटी में नीचे, कावेरी सदियों से अपना रास्ता खुद काटती आई थी, कण्णमबीडु के खेतों को चीरती, टीपू के उस पहले सपने को अनसुना करती, जिसका अधूरा बाँध बस यादों और शिलालेख में जिंदा था।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of a council table with British and Mysore officials around it
panels.action: Around a long table, British engineers and Mysore officials sit in heated discussion, some leaning forward, some skeptical, as Visvesvaraya stands at one end with rolled plans, while a portrait of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV hangs watchfully on the wall.

dialogue.text: The project had to cross not just a river, but a tangle of doubts, rival claims, and imperial caution. Could Mysore be trusted with so much water, so much concrete, so much risk?

i18n.hi: परियोजना को सिर्फ नदी नहीं, शक, झगड़े और हुकूमती एहतियात की उलझन भी पार करनी थी। क्या मैसूर पर इतना पानी, इतना कंक्रीट, इतना ख़तरा भरोसे के काबिल था?

panels.shot: close-up on Visvesvaraya’s face as he addresses unseen critics, jaw set
panels.action: Visvesvaraya stands in a formal meeting room, shoulders squared, speaking towards off-frame officials with measured intensity, while his hand rests on a thick bundle of technical reports bound in cloth.

dialogue.speaker: M. Visvesvaraya
dialogue.text: We store floods, release measured flows, and share them by agreement. Without storage, all lose.

i18n.hi: हम बाढ़ रोकेंगे, नापतौल से पानी छोड़ेंगे, और समझौते से बाँटेंगे। बिना भंडार, सब हारे।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of the Maharaja signing the project sanction with a ceremonial pen
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, dressed in regal attire, bends over a formal document on a carved desk, carefully signing the sanction for the KRS project as Visvesvaraya stands respectfully to one side, watching with quiet satisfaction.

dialogue.text: In 1911, with a steady hand and a stroke of ink, the Maharaja approved a dam that would submerge Kannambadi and lift Mysore’s fortunes, binding his name to a wall yet to rise.

i18n.hi: १९११ में, ठहरती कलम और स्याही की एक लकीर से, महाराजा ने उस बाँध को मंजूर किया जो कण्णमबीडु को डुबोकर मैसूर की किस्मत उठाएगा, और उनका नाम एक अभी न बनी दीवार से जोड़ देगा।

panels.shot: sweeping panoramic shot of early construction, with workers swarming over foundations
panels.action: On a vast riverbed cleared of water by coffer dams, hundreds of workers move like ants among stone blocks and scaffolding, while primitive cranes and carts haul materials; Visvesvaraya stands on a temporary platform with a field notebook, overseeing the early stages.

dialogue.text: By the early 1910s, Kannambadi was no longer only a village; it was a camp of surveyors, masons, and labourers, carving foundations into hard rock under a Diwan who believed order was also an engineering tool.

i18n.hi: १९१० के शुरुआती सालों में, कण्णमबीडु सिर्फ गाँव नहीं रहा; वह नापतौलियों, राज मिस्त्रियों और मज़दूरों का डेरा बना, जो सख्त चट्टान में नींव काट रहे थे, ऐसे दीवान के नीचे जो अनुशासन को भी इंजीनियरिंग का औज़ार मानता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Visvesvaraya examining a sample of surki mortar in his hand
panels.action: Visvesvaraya stands beside a pile of materials, lifting a chunk of reddish surki mortar and turning it critically in his hand as an engineer beside him holds a clipboard; behind them, workers mix mortar in large pits.

dialogue.text: Cement was scarce and costly. The dam would stand on surki mortar—lime and brick dust—tested, retested, and arranged with such discipline that every joint became a calculation, not a guess.

i18n.hi: सीमेंट कम और महँगा था। बाँध सुरखी — चूना और ईंट की धूल — पर खड़ा होना था, जिसकी बार‑बार परख हुई, और इतनी सख्ती से जमाया गया कि हर जोड़ अंदाज़ नहीं, हिसाब बना।

panels.shot: detailed mid-shot of engineers around a scale model of the dam with crest gates
panels.action: In a temporary site office, Visvesvaraya and a small group of engineers stand around a wooden scale model of the dam, its top lined with miniature metal crest gates, while Visvesvaraya points to how the gates rise and fall.

dialogue.text: On his drawing boards, the wall did more than block water. With automatic crest gates, it could lift itself in flood and fall in drought, turning the river’s moods into a measured, mechanical rhythm.

i18n.hi: उसकी तख्तियों पर, दीवार सिर्फ पानी नहीं रोकती थी। अपने ऑटोमैटिक क्रेस्ट गेटों से, बाढ़ में खुद ऊपर उठती, सूखे में नीची हो जाती, नदी के मिजाज को नापा‑तौला, यांत्रिक ताल बना देती।

panels.shot: close-up of the actual crest gate mechanism installed on the partially built dam, gleaming in the sun
panels.action: A section of the KRS dam’s crest shows a heavy metal gate seated in its grooves, its hinges and counterweights precise and clean, while the calm river laps just below the masonry.

dialogue.text: These were not imported fantasies. They were practical, tested devices, building on Visvesvaraya’s earlier work, designed so that no inattentive human hand could delay crucial releases.

i18n.hi: ये कोई बाहर की ख्याली चीजें नहीं थीं। ये आजमाए हुए, काम के औज़ार थे, विश्वेश्वरैया के पहले के काम पर खड़े, ऐसे बनाए कि कोई सुस्त हाथ अहम पानी रोक न सके।

panels.shot: somber mid-wide of villagers watching as markings are placed on their soon-to-be-submerged homes
panels.action: At the edge of Kannambadi, villagers stand silently as survey workers chalk marks on house walls and trees, indicating future submergence levels, with the rising dam visible in the distant background.

dialogue.text: Yet every foot the dam rose was a line higher on the walls of Kannambadi’s homes. Progress meant packing memories into bundles, watching fields measured not for harvest, but for depth.

i18n.hi: पर बाँध का हर नया फुट, कण्णमबीडु के घरों की दीवारों पर एक ऊँची लकीर था। तरक्की का मतलब था यादों को गठरियों में बाँधना, खेतों को फसलों नहीं, गहराई के नाप से देखना।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of the Maharaja and Visvesvaraya walking along the half-built dam at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, with lanterns flickering, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and Visvesvaraya walk slowly along the unfinished crest, workers resting in the background, the river a dark band below as they speak in low tones.

dialogue.speaker: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
dialogue.text: We lift this state, Sir, yet we drown a village. Let us be worthy of both.

i18n.hi: हम इस रियासत को उठाते हैं, सर, पर एक गाँव डुबोते भी हैं। हमें दोनों के काबिल होना होगा।

panels.shot: montage-like wide with superimposed sense of time passing: changing equipment, growing wall, different seasons
panels.action: The dam wall appears in three overlapping stages across the frame: low in one corner with hand tools, mid-level with more cranes, and near full height with broader crest, while monsoon clouds, summer heat, and clear skies suggest the passing years.

dialogue.text: War years, price shocks, and supply delays stretched the work. But stone by stone, season by season, the structure rose above the valley, until by 1924 its masonry bulk commanded the river.

i18n.hi: जंग के साल, भावों के झटके और रसद की देरी ने काम खींच दिया। पर पत्थर‑पत्थर, मौसम‑मौसम, ढांचा घाटी के ऊपर उठता गया, जब तक १९२४ तक उसकी पक्की देह नदी पर हावी न हो गई।

panels.shot: grand wide shot of the reservoir beginning to fill, water creeping over former fields
panels.action: Water spreads slowly across the basin behind the completed main wall, covering former fields and trees that now protrude like dark fingers from the rising surface, while distant hills reflect in the new lake.

dialogue.text: As sluices closed and gates took their positions, the old Kaveri narrowed and a new sheet of water began to spread, swallowing furrows and footpaths, birthing Krishna Raja Sagara, the sea of the Maharaja.

i18n.hi: जैसे ही फाटक बंद हुए और गेट अपनी जगह टिके, पुरानी कावेरी सिकुड़ गई और नया पानी का चादर फैलने लगी, क्यारियाँ और पगडंडियाँ निगलते हुए, कृष्ण राज सागर को जन्म देती — महाराजा का समुंदर।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of irrigation canals carrying water into dry fields, farmers looking on
panels.action: Newly built canals branch out from the reservoir, clear water flowing briskly into parched fields where farmers watch with cautious hope, some stepping barefoot into the channels as the first flows reach their land.

dialogue.text: From the reservoir’s edge, water ran in orderly lines, not wild floods but timed releases, turning Mandya’s soils into cane and paddy, and promising that drought would no longer be an annual guest.

i18n.hi: झील के किनारे से, पानी सीधी कतारों में भागा, जंगली बाढ़ नहीं, समय बाँधे बहाव, जिसने मांड्या की मिट्टी को गन्ना और धान में बदला, और वादा किया कि सूखा हर साल का मेहमान नहीं रहेगा।

panels.shot: medium shot of urban Mysore with a new water tower and pipes being laid
panels.action: In Mysore city, workers lay metal water pipes along a street, while a new elevated water tower rises behind colonial and traditional buildings, and townspeople watch the unfamiliar infrastructure with curiosity.

dialogue.text: Beyond the fields, pipes carried KRS water into Mysore’s taps, joining the dam to the city’s daily life—a hidden link between a palace decision, a rural valley, and a glass of drinking water.

i18n.hi: खेतों से आगे, पाइप केआरएस का पानी मैसूर के नलों तक लाए, बाँध को शहर की रोज़मर्रा से जोड़ते — महल की एक मंजूरी, देहाती घाटी, और ग्लास के पानी के बीच छुपी कड़ी।

panels.shot: close shot of a commemorative plaque at the dam site mentioning Tipu’s earlier intent and the present project
panels.action: A stone plaque is set into the dam-side structure, its carved surface showing a respectful reference to Tipu Sultan’s earlier dam intention and an inscription honouring the current project under Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and M. Visvesvaraya.

dialogue.text: Near the crest, stone letters recalled Tipu’s unfulfilled plan, linking past intent to present achievement, and quietly reminding visitors that history often moves by delayed dreams and different hands.

i18n.hi: शिखर के पास, पत्थर की अक्षरों ने टीपू की अधूरी योजना को याद किया, पुरानी नीयत को नई कामयाबी से जोड़ते, और चुपचाप बताते कि इतिहास अक्सर टले हुए सपनों और बदले हुए हाथों से चलता है।

panels.shot: high-angle shot in the late 1920s of both men overlooking the fully formed lake and far-off green fields
panels.action: In the late 1920s, an older Visvesvaraya and Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV stand side by side on the completed dam, the vast, calm lake on one side and a distant patchwork of irrigated green fields on the other, both men silent and reflective.

dialogue.text: By the close of the 1920s and into the early 1930s, the KRS stood not only as masonry finished, gates adjusted, and canals refined, but as proof that a princely state could plan like a modern power.

i18n.hi: १९२० के आखिर और १९३० के शुरुआती सालों तक, केआरएस सिर्फ पूरा हुआ बाँध, ठीक किए गेट और सधे नहर नहीं था, बल्कि सबूत था कि एक रियासत भी किसी आधुनिक ताकत की तरह योजना बना सकती है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Visvesvaraya’s lined face, eyes reflecting both the water and the memory of resistance overcome
panels.action: Visvesvaraya’s weathered face fills the frame, his eyes catching the glint of the reservoir and the distant outline of the dam, his expression a mix of pride, fatigue, and awareness of the costs that lay beneath the water.

dialogue.text: The dam did not end scarcity, nor erase displacement. But it carved a path where imagination, calculation, and public need held together long enough to change a river’s fate—and ours.

i18n.hi: बाँध ने न कमी पूरी तरह मिटाई, न उजड़न। पर उसने एक राह काटी, जहाँ खयाल, हिसाब और जनता की ज़रूरत, इतने समय तक साथ रहे कि एक नदी की किस्मत — और हमारी — बदल गई।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Mysore Turned the Kaveri into a Modern Sea
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे मैसूर ने कावेरी को बनाया नया समुंदर
